Skill Access

Read the linked rule alongside the procedure below.

  1. Check Primary and Secondary access for the current Fighter type and gang.
  2. Keep the any-skill exception on advancement 12 separate from normal access.

Skill Access

Primary and Secondary skill access depends on the model type and gang. An advancement result of 12 can also select skills exclusive to a particular gang or Inner Circle, and skills normally unavailable to the model's type or subtype.

Buying, selling and equipment sets

Manage credits and TP, exclusive access, weapon slots and multiple equipment sets. Check each Vehicle’s own equipment limits.

Buying Equipment

Read the linked rule alongside the procedure below.

  1. Separate the always-available gang list from external access requiring a visit.
  2. Check exclusive E access, credit/TP costs and expiry of unused TP.
Needs review: the linked rule contains unresolved details. Do not infer missing values or choice directions.

Buying Equipment

Recruitment and equipment transactions take place in the Trading Post step of roster updates. Gang equipment lists are always available; external Trading Posts require at least one Visit Trading Post action. Exclusive equipment marked E may be bought only if it appears on the model's equipment list. Each transaction spends both credits and TP; unused TP expires at the end of the step.

Selling Equipment

Read the linked rule alongside the procedure below.

  1. Select a stash item to sell and remove it from the stash.
  2. Use half value with a minimum of 5 credits while checking unresolved odd-value rounding.
Needs review: the linked rule contains unresolved details. Do not infer missing values or choice directions.

Selling Equipment

Items in the Stash may be sold: remove the item and receive half its credit value, with a minimum of 5 credits.

Redistributing Equipment

Read the linked rule alongside the procedure below.

  1. Choose to discard, move to stash or transfer to another model.
  2. Check exclusive E recipient eligibility and the need for multiple sets above three slots.

Redistributing Equipment

Equipment may be discarded, transferred to the Stash or given to another model. Equipment marked E must appear on the recipient's equipment list. Models owning more than three weapons require multiple equipment-set cards.

Weapon Limits

Read the linked rule alongside the procedure below.

  1. Count a Fighter’s limit as three slots and starred weapons as two slots.
  2. Check grenade exclusion, one accessory per weapon and Vehicle-specific limits.

Weapon Limits

A Fighter may carry at most three weapons. Grenades count as equipment and do not use weapon slots; a weapon marked * uses two slots. Vehicle weapon limits are specified in each Vehicle entry. Each weapon can have at most one accessory.

Equipment Sets

Read the linked rule alongside the procedure below.

  1. Keep XP, injuries and advancements shared across all cards for one model.
  2. Count shared equipment only once and use one set in battle.
Needs review: the linked rule contains unresolved details. Do not infer missing values or choice directions.

Equipment Sets

Every model may have multiple equipment-set cards at no extra cost. An item may be shared across sets but is purchased and counted towards roster value only once. A model has one roster entry, with injuries and advancements shared by all cards. Use only one card in a battle. Random selection must prevent selecting the same model twice and must not let the player directly choose its set.

Campaign structure, succession and enduring gangs

Review cycles, Leader succession, campaign awards and rehiring into another campaign. Apply campaign-specific conditions alongside core rules.

Leader Succession

Read the linked rule alongside the procedure below.

  1. Find candidates among non-Loner Champions, then Loner Champions, then other eligible Fighters.
  2. Within the first eligible group, use Leadership, then total XP, then player choice.

Leader Succession

Choose a successor from non-Loner Champions first, then Loner Champions, then other eligible Fighters. Within each group, decide by highest Leadership, then total XP, then player choice. The new Leader keeps its characteristics, skills and special rules and gains the type and access appropriate to its role.

Enduring Gangs

Read the linked rule alongside the procedure below.

  1. After the previous Leader retires, choose an eligible existing Fighter as the new Leader.
  2. Pay to rehire and retain XP, injuries, equipment and skills; record one chosen Triumph.

Enduring Gangs

A gang that completes a campaign may continue as an Enduring Gang. Its previous Leader retires, and an existing Fighter becomes the new Leader. Rehired models must be paid for and retain XP, injuries, equipment and skills. One chosen previous Triumph benefit applies only to the immediately following campaign.

Core Campaign cycles and rewards

Separate Occupation, Downtime and Takeover phases and their rewards.

  1. Record the default seven cycles as three Occupation, one Downtime and three Takeover.
  2. Record one starting Settlement and one random territory; do not stake the starting Settlement.
  3. Check the current phase before awarding credits and Reputation.
  4. Use the 250 Downtime credits for new recruits and gang equipment at that time; do not retain unused credits.
Needs review: the relationship between player count, total territory count and a separate 2D6 notation is unresolved. Distinguish D66 territory types from the number in the territory pool and agree with the Arbitrator.

Core Campaign

The default campaign lasts seven cycles: three Occupation, one Downtime and three Takeover. Start with one Settlement that cannot be staked or lost and one random territory. In Occupation, victory grants 2D3×10 credits and +1 Reputation; defeat, a draw or a completed Side Job grants D3×10 credits. In Takeover, victory grants 2D6×10 credits and +2 Reputation; defeat, a draw or a completed Side Job grants D6×10 credits. Losing territory costs 1 Reputation. The 250-credit Downtime allowance may be spent only then on new recruits and gang equipment; none can be retained.

Territory income, boons and stakes

Distinguish ownership effects from effects in a battle fought over the territory.

  1. Separate each territory’s income from options replacing that income.
  2. Separate ongoing ownership boons from effects when the territory is staked.
  3. Record choices and credit changes when collecting income.
Needs review: do not generalise Rogue Doc Shop assistance to every kind of assistance beyond recovery. The AP sign/direction for Synth Still and whether Old Ruins Long Range includes Short Range remain unresolved.

Settlement

Collect 15 credits as income. Instead, forgo this income to discount the recruitment cost of one Ganger by 25 credits, to a minimum of 0. A starting Settlement cannot be staked or lost.

Bullet Den

Income: 15 credits. If the gang has no Ammo-Jack, it may instead discount the recruitment cost of one by 30 credits. In a battle for this territory, each gang may perform one Reload as a Free action per round.

Rogue Doc Shop

Income: 15 credits. If the gang has no Rogue Doc, it may instead discount the recruitment cost of one by 30 credits. In a battle for this territory, a Fighter assisting Recovery rolls two Injury dice instead of one.

Drinking Hole

Income: 15 credits. If the gang has no Hive Watcher, it may instead discount the recruitment cost of one by 30 credits. Ranged weapons cannot be used in the first round of a battle for this territory.

Mess Shack

Income: 15 credits. If the gang has no Slopper, it may instead discount the recruitment cost of one by 30 credits. All models gain +1 Leadership in a battle for this territory.

Fence Hangout

Income: 15 credits. If the gang has no Dome Runner, it may instead discount the recruitment cost of one by 30 credits. In a battle for this territory, add D3×10 credits to the reward for completing a Side Job.

Bounty Den

Income: 25 credits. Each player generates one additional Side Job in a battle for this territory.

Generatorium

Income: 15 credits. Gain +1 Reputation while controlling this territory; remove this bonus if it is lost. Visibility (X) does not apply in a battle for this territory.

Corpse Farm

Income: 25 credits. In a battle for this territory, gain 10 credits for each enemy model taken Out of Action.

Tunnels

Income: 20 credits. Apply Tunnel Warfare in a battle for this territory.

Tech Bazaar

Income: 15 credits. While controlling this territory, gain +1 TP per post-cycle sequence and always have Trading Post access. Blast and Template weapons cannot be used in the first round of a battle for this territory.

Promethium Cache

Income: 15 credits, or forgo it to add three free Hazard Suits to the Stash. In a battle for this territory, reduce the X in Blaze (X+) by 1, for example from 5+ to 4+.

Collapsed Dome

Income: 20 credits. In a battle for this territory, a natural 1 on an Agility test also inflicts a Str –, AP –, L1 hit on that model. It wounds automatically and allows no save.

Bone Shrine

Income: 25 credits. In a battle for this territory, the defender places a shrine marker within 6 inches of the battlefield centre. Fighters may control the shrine as an objective to gain XP.

Mine Workings

Income: 20 credits, or forgo it to add two free Respirators to the Stash. Apply Visibility (18 inches) in a battle for this territory.

Gambling Den

Income: 15 credits. Gain +1 Reputation while controlling this territory; remove this bonus if it is lost. In a battle for this territory, each player may re-roll one die once per battle.

Synth Still

Income: 20 credits. In a battle for this territory, Toxin (X+) weapons receive an AP adjustment of 1. The direction of the signed AP adjustment needs verification.

Old Ruins

Income: 20 credits. In a battle for this territory, a model within a weapon's Long Range and not in cover increases its Save characteristic by 1. The distinction between Long Range and Short Range for this effect needs verification.

Fighting Pit

Income: 25 credits. In a battle for this territory, a model gains +1 XP when its melee attack makes an enemy Seriously Injured/Damaged or takes it Out of Action.

Triumphs and next-campaign boons

Check award criteria separately from the boon chosen for the next campaign.

  1. Check awards for final territories, inflicted OOA, Wealth, battles and Reputation.
  2. Break ties by Wealth; remaining ties share the award.
  3. An enduring gang chooses one boon, applying it only in the next campaign.

Dominator

Awarded for the most territories at campaign end. Break ties by higher Wealth; if still tied, all tied gangs win. If an Enduring Gang chooses this previous Triumph's benefit, it starts the next campaign with one additional territory. The benefit applies only to the immediately following campaign.

Slaughterer

Awarded for the most enemy models taken Out of Action over the campaign. Break ties by higher Wealth; if still tied, all tied gangs win. If an Enduring Gang chooses this previous Triumph's benefit, after gang creation distribute a total of 9 XP among models rehired from the previous gang, at most 3 XP each. The benefit applies only to the immediately following campaign.

Creditor

Awarded for the highest Wealth at campaign end. Break ties by higher Wealth; if still tied, all tied gangs win. If an Enduring Gang chooses this previous Triumph's benefit, add 100 credits to its starting funds; these may be spent during gang creation. The benefit applies only to the immediately following campaign.

Warmonger

Awarded for the most battles fought over the campaign. Break ties by higher Wealth; if still tied, all tied gangs win. If an Enduring Gang chooses this previous Triumph's benefit, it starts with +2 Reputation and chooses attacker or defender in its first battle regardless of who issued the challenge. The benefit applies only to the immediately following campaign.

Powerbroker

Awarded for the highest Reputation at campaign end. Break ties by higher Wealth; if still tied, all tied gangs win. If an Enduring Gang chooses this previous Triumph's benefit, it starts with one free Ammo-Jack, Dome Runner, Hive Watcher, Rogue Doc or Slopper, including all options. The benefit applies only to the immediately following campaign.

Cycle challenges, refusal and stakes

Check the campaign phase and challenge order before choosing the stake.

  1. By default each player issues one challenge per cycle. The first cycle order is random; later cycles use ascending gang Rating, with a roll-off for ties.
  2. The challenger is the attacker. In Occupation, stake unclaimed territory first, and opponent-owned territory only when the pool is empty. Takeover uses opponent-owned stakes.
  3. Refusal normally transfers the stake immediately to the challenger. Check no-loss refusal exceptions for an additional challenge after issuing one’s own, and for receiving at least two challenges that cycle.
  4. Additional challenges are possible after completing one’s own battles if time remains.
  5. The winner gains or retains the stake. An Occupation draw leaves an unclaimed stake in the pool; a Takeover draw leaves it with the previous owner.

Core Campaign

The default campaign lasts seven cycles: three Occupation, one Downtime and three Takeover. Start with one Settlement that cannot be staked or lost and one random territory. In Occupation, victory grants 2D3×10 credits and +1 Reputation; defeat, a draw or a completed Side Job grants D3×10 credits. In Takeover, victory grants 2D6×10 credits and +2 Reputation; defeat, a draw or a completed Side Job grants D6×10 credits. Losing territory costs 1 Reputation. The 250-credit Downtime allowance may be spent only then on new recruits and gang equipment; none can be retained.

Recording recruits and equipment gained from territory

The discounted amount paid can differ from a model’s normal value.

  1. Apply ownership boons while the territory is controlled; collect income in the post-cycle income step.
  2. Use the normal full recruit cost for Rating and Wealth of a discounted recruit; do not substitute the free/discounted price.
  3. Buy equipment not included in the boon normally or provide it from the stash.
  4. Retain previously gained recruits and equipment after losing the territory. Sell boon equipment in a later post-cycle.
  5. Check the scope of battlefield effects on all participants in battles fought over that territory.

Core Campaign

The default campaign lasts seven cycles: three Occupation, one Downtime and three Takeover. Start with one Settlement that cannot be staked or lost and one random territory. In Occupation, victory grants 2D3×10 credits and +1 Reputation; defeat, a draw or a completed Side Job grants D3×10 credits. In Takeover, victory grants 2D6×10 credits and +2 Reputation; defeat, a draw or a completed Side Job grants D6×10 credits. Losing territory costs 1 Reputation. The 250-credit Downtime allowance may be spent only then on new recruits and gang equipment; none can be retained.

Deployments, objectives, crews and side jobs

Check who rolls on each table, then open the result. Unresolved details such as deployment maps remain marked for review.

Deployments

Check the roller and individual results together.

  1. Open the individual entry for the D6 result.
  2. Confirm targets, distances, victory conditions and reward timing before battle.
Verify deployment maps and unresolved areas without inventing geometry.

Deployments

The challenger rolls a D6 to generate the deployment type. Deployment areas with unresolved boundaries require manual verification.

Sniping Range

The roll-off winner chooses a battlefield edge; the opponent uses the opposite edge. The deployment distance is 12 inches. Its exact relationship to the centre line and deployment zones needs verification.

Face Off

The roll-off winner chooses a battlefield edge; the opponent uses the opposite edge. The deployment distance is 9 inches. Its exact relationship to the centre line and deployment zones needs verification.

Stand Off

The roll-off winner chooses a battlefield edge; the opponent uses the opposite edge. The deployment distance is 6 inches. Its exact relationship to the centre line and deployment zones needs verification.

Ambush

The defender deploys within 6 inches of the battlefield centre. The attacker deploys at least 12 inches from the centre.

Free For All

The roll-off winner chooses a battlefield quarter; the opponent uses the opposite quarter. Each deploys in its quarter at least 9 inches from the centre.

Chance Encounter

The roll-off winner uses areas within 9 inches of a chosen corner and the diagonally opposite corner. The opponent uses the other two corners. Each gang divides its crew as evenly as possible between its two deployment zones.

Objectives

Check the roller and individual results together.

  1. Open the individual entry for the D6 result.
  2. Confirm targets, distances, victory conditions and reward timing before battle.
Needs review: in Object Lesson, the timing of a drawn ending when neither side reaches 10VP remains unresolved. Do not infer an automatic ending condition.

Objectives

The challenger rolls a D6 to generate the battle's main objective. Victory rewards depend on the campaign phase.

King of the Hive

Place one objective at the centre. At Check For Victory, controlling it grants 1 VP; the first player to reach 3 VP wins. If only one gang has models remaining on the battlefield, that gang wins; if neither does, the battle is a draw.

Turf War

From round 3 onwards, at Check For Victory, a player wins if only their gang has a model that is not Seriously Injured/Damaged within 9 inches of the centre. If only one gang has models remaining on the battlefield, that gang wins; if neither does, the battle is a draw.

Tunnel Clash

Place one objective at the centre. Starting with the roll-off winner, each player adds one more, at least 6 inches from other objectives and battlefield edges. At Check For Victory, controlling two objectives grants 1 VP; the first player to reach 3 VP wins. If only one gang has models remaining, that gang wins; if neither does, the battle is a draw.

Object Lesson

At Check For Victory, gain 1 VP per enemy taken Out of Action this round. Gain +1 VP if it was a Leader, Champion or Brute and +1 VP if taken out by Fight, Coup de Grâce or Sabotage; these bonuses can combine. The first player to reach 10 VP wins. If only one gang has models remaining, that gang wins; if neither does, the battle is a draw. The ending point for a draw before reaching the VP target needs verification.

Flank ‘em

The attacker places an objective 6 inches inwards from the midpoint of its chosen battlefield edge; the defender does the same at the opposite edge. At Check For Victory, controlling both objectives grants 1 VP; the first player to reach 3 VP wins. If only one gang has models remaining, that gang wins; if neither does, the battle is a draw.

Burn Them Out

Starting with the defender, players alternate placing three objectives each in the opposing deployment zone, at least 6 inches apart. At Check For Victory, controlling an objective in the opposing zone grants 1 VP and removes it. The first player to reach 2 VP wins; if both have at least 2 VP, the battle is a draw. If only one gang has models remaining, that gang wins; if neither does, the battle is a draw.

Side Jobs

Check the roller and individual results together.

  1. Open the individual entry for the D6 result.
  2. Confirm targets, distances, victory conditions and reward timing before battle.

Side Jobs

Each player rolls a D6 to generate their own Side Job. Side Job rewards depend on the campaign phase.

Stitch ‘em Up

During Coup de Grâce, a Fighter may plant evidence on a Seriously Injured enemy Fighter instead of making the Strength roll-off. Complete this Side Job by planting evidence on at least one enemy Fighter during the battle; it remains complete even if that enemy leaves the battlefield.

The Package

After deployment, give the package to one friendly Fighter. From round 3 onwards, at Check For Victory, remove the marker and complete this Side Job if its carrier is touching the opposing deployment zone. If that zone has no battlefield edge, complete it at the battlefield centre instead.

Settle a Score

After deployment, randomly select and openly identify one deployed enemy model that is not the Leader. At Check For Victory, complete this Side Job if that model is Out of Action or has left the battlefield for any reason.

Crippling Strike

At Check For Victory, complete this Side Job if at least half the opposing models are Seriously Injured/Damaged or Engaged.

Spread Unrest

Complete this Side Job when an Active friendly Fighter that is not a Beast performs Graffiti (Double) in the opposing deployment zone. If there is no opposing deployment zone, perform it within 6 inches of the centre. Completion remains valid even if the Fighter leaves the battlefield.

Protect the Future

After deployment, randomly select and openly identify one deployed friendly Prospect. If the starting crew has no Prospect, select a Ganger. Complete this Side Job if that Fighter remains on the battlefield when the battle ends.

Crew

Check the roller and individual results together.

  1. Open the individual entry for the D6 result.
  2. Confirm targets, distances, victory conditions and reward timing before battle.

Crew

The challenged player rolls a D6 to generate both gangs' starting crews and reinforcements.

Escalating Engagement

Both starting crews use Hybrid (3+D3). Both gangs have Reinforcements (5), with D3 models arriving each round from round 1.

Hold Nothing Back!

Both starting crews use Custom (10).

Patrol

Both starting crews use Hybrid (3+4).

Surprise Attack

The attacker's starting crew uses Hybrid (4+4). The defender uses Custom (3) and Reinforcements (7), with D3 models arriving each round from round 1.

Strike Force

Both starting crews use Custom (5).

Scouting Force

Both starting crews use Hybrid (D3+5).

Weapon trait reference

Link profile traits to their individual rules. Distinguish changes to core procedures from additional effects.

Firing, ammunition and arcs

Check each profile trait’s conditions, values and timing.

  1. Read every linked trait rather than relying on the profile name.
  2. Distinguish natural hit/wound results, success, target type and trigger limits.
Needs review: extra rolls and Reload interactions involving Ammo(X+) and Out of Ammo remain unresolved. Do not infer extra dice or automatic restoration beyond the verified ammo-symbol rule.

Ammo (X+)

After shooting, make an Ammo check on a D6, succeeding on X or higher. When used with Rapid Fire, a failed check counts as 1 additional Ammo symbol.

Arc (X)

Only models within firing arc X can be selected as targets.

Assault

After performing Dash, the fighter can make a Free Shoot with this weapon.

Blast (3"/5")

Centre a marker of the indicated size on the target. On a successful hit, it stays in place; on a miss, scatter it D6 inches in the direction indicated, stopping at impassable terrain or a battlefield edge. If the Scatter die shows Hit and the distance roll is 1, centre it on the firer. Every model even partially beneath the marker suffers 1 automatic hit. For additional Rapid Fire hits, scatter additional markers from the first marker's final position.

Combi

Choose a profile before performing Shoot or Aimed Shot. Both profiles can be fired simultaneously at the same target, with -1 to hit for each.

Independent

Cannot be fired directly. It fires in addition when another ranged weapon attacks, and can choose a different target. It always hits at BS 4+, unaffected by the user's BS, equipment or special rules, and gains no benefit from Aimed Shot.

Limited

Once Out of Ammo, the weapon cannot be reloaded or used again during that battle.

Rapid Fire (X)

Roll up to X Firepower dice and inflict hits equal to the total bullet symbols. Any Ammo symbol makes the weapon Out of Ammo; multiple Ammo symbols prevent further use that battle. A failed Ammo check counts as 1 additional Ammo symbol. Hits after the first can be allocated to enemies within 3 inches of the original target that are also within range and line of sight.

Reckless

For shooting, randomly select a target from all models, including friendlies, within the firer's range and line of sight. In melee, randomly allocate attacks among all Engaged models, including friendlies.

Reliable

Each round, cancel the first Ammo symbol or 1 failed Ammo check.

Scarce (X+)

Reload does not automatically succeed. Roll a D6: on X or higher, reload successfully. On a failure, remain Out of Ammo and try again in a later activation.

Single Shot

Can fire 1 shot per battle. Immediately becomes Out of Ammo and cannot be reloaded by any means.

Smoke

Can target a point instead of an enemy. Leave an infinitely tall, line-of-sight-blocking smoke cloud at the final Blast position, stopping at the edge of any terrain it contacts. During the Reinforcement step of each End phase, roll a D6: on a 5+, it remains; otherwise remove it. Models hit by a Smoke grenade are neither Wounded nor Suppressed.

Template

Place the teardrop template with its narrow end touching the firer and the target beneath it. Every model even partially touched is automatically hit, with no hit roll. When used with Light in melee, automatically hit 1 enemy. With Rapid Fire, only the closest model suffers the number of hits indicated by the Firepower dice; all other models suffer 1 hit each.

Twin-linked

When shooting, the Firepower dice can be re-rolled. Re-roll all of them, rather than selecting individual dice.

Unstable

On a natural 1 to hit, the user suffers an automatic hit using the weapon's profile, and no other models are hit. For a weapon that does not make a hit roll, roll a separate D6 before resolving the attack.

Melee, attacks and defence

Check each profile trait’s conditions, values and timing.

  1. Read every linked trait rather than relying on the profile name.
  2. Distinguish natural hit/wound results, success, target type and trigger limits.

Additional Attacks (X)

During the model's activation, make X additional attacks in addition to its normal melee attacks, but only if this weapon was not selected as the Primary or Secondary weapon.

Backstab

Gain +1 Strength if the target is Engaged with 2 or more models.

Heavy

A ranged weapon can only be fired with Braced Shot. A melee weapon cannot be selected as a Secondary weapon or used alongside another Secondary weapon.

Lance

A Mounted fighter gains +1 Strength when attacking as part of a Charge.

Lance-bomb

Use the Primed profile for the first successful hit in a battle and the Spent profile for all subsequent hits.

Light

Can be used as a Primary or Secondary melee weapon, but makes only 1 attack regardless of Attacks, skills or traits. If it also has Template, automatically hit 1 enemy in melee without placing a template.

Melee

Used to make attacks while Engaged.

Paired (X)

Cannot be selected as a Secondary weapon or used alongside another Secondary weapon. Gain +X Attacks when selected as the Primary weapon.

Parry

Gain +1 Save when using this as a Primary or Secondary melee weapon. Multiple instances do not stack.

Ram

Can only be used during an activation in which the fighter Charged.

Shield

Gain +1 Save against ranged attacks while equipped with one or more weapons with this trait. Multiple instances do not stack.

Unwieldy

When used in melee, set Initiative to 1 before applying other modifiers.

Wounds, injuries and conditions

Check each profile trait’s conditions, values and timing.

  1. Read every linked trait rather than relying on the profile name.
  2. Distinguish natural hit/wound results, success, target type and trigger limits.
Needs review: the relationship between W lost, L and injury dice for Damage(X), and the Ready restriction timing and Blind duration for Flash, remain unresolved.

Blaze (X+)

If the wound roll is X or higher, inflict 1 additional hit using the first hit's profile, even if that wound roll failed. Additional hits cannot trigger Blaze again. If multiple Blaze traits apply, use only 1 instance with the lowest X.

Breaching (X+)

If the attack successfully wounds and its wound roll is X or higher, no Armour Save is allowed.

Concussive (X+)

If the attack successfully wounds and its wound roll is X or higher, the target suffers -1 Initiative until the end of its next activation.

Cursed

A hit target gains Insanity if it fails a Willpower check. If the firer rolls a natural 1 to hit, the firer also gains Insanity if they fail a Willpower check.

Damage (X)

On a successful wound, the target loses X Wounds instead of the normal amount.

Drag

If a hit target is not Out of Action after resolving the attack, roll a D6. If the result equals or exceeds the attacker's Strength, drag the target D3 inches towards the attacker. If it contacts another model, both move together for the remaining distance. This can cause a fall. If the target ends within 1 inch of an enemy, move it the shortest distance into Engaged contact.

Flash

The target makes an Initiative check instead of a wound roll. On a failure, it becomes Blind and loses Ready. If it has no Ready marker, it cannot gain a new one. Until its next activation, its melee attacks hit only on a natural 6.

Gas

No Armour Save is allowed. A Respirator grants a 5+ Invulnerable save against Gas wounds.

Graviton Pulse

Models beneath the Blast marker make a Strength check instead of a wound roll. On a failure, they are Wounded with no Armour Save allowed. Leave the marker in place as difficult terrain. At the start of each End phase, roll a D6: on a 5+, it remains for the next round; otherwise remove it.

Knockback (X+)

If a fighter is hit with a hit roll of X or higher, move it 1 inch directly away from the firer. This can trigger a falling test or break engagement. For Blast, roll a separate D6 for each target hit by each marker; on X or higher, move it away from the marker's centre. Do not move it if the move would enter impassable terrain, cross a battlefield edge or enter within 1 inch of an enemy.

Rad-phage

A fighter that suffers an unsaved wound becomes Rad Poisoned, reducing Toughness by 1 to a minimum of 1.

Rending (X+)

On a natural wound roll of X or higher, improve that attack's AP by +1, for example from -1 to -2.

Shock (X+)

A successful hit with a hit roll of X or higher automatically wounds. Treat its wound roll as a natural 6 when resolving other traits.

Shred (X+)

If the attack successfully wounds and its wound roll is X or higher, increase that attack's Lethality by +1.

Toxin (X+)

Against fighters, wound on X+ instead of comparing Strength and Toughness. Against vehicles, wound only on a natural 6 instead of comparing Strength and Toughness.

Web

No Armour Save is allowed, but an Invulnerable save can be made. Fighters become Webbed instead of losing Wounds.

Equipment, attachments and slots

Check each profile trait’s conditions, values and timing.

  1. Read every linked trait rather than relying on the profile name.
  2. Distinguish natural hit/wound results, success, target type and trigger limits.

Auxiliary

Used attached to another weapon; cannot be used on its own. Does not count towards the three-weapon limit.

Power Pack

Does not count towards the maximum number of carried weapons, but a fighter can have at most 2 weapons with this trait.

Quick sheets

N26 · Reference

Dice, tests and checks

  1. WS/BS: succeed on D6 at or above the target. Natural 1 fails and natural 6 succeeds.
  2. Ld/Cl/Wil/Int: succeed on a 2D6 total at or below the characteristic.
  3. Other characteristic checks: succeed on D6 at or below the characteristic.
  4. D66: the first D6 is tens and the second units. A 2 then 4 gives 24.
  5. Normally round division up. Reroll a die at most once and keep the new result.
D3 conversion remains for review.
N26 · Setup

Seven pre-battle steps

  1. ① Issue the challenge and agree the territory stake.
  2. ② Determine the scenario.
  3. ③ Build the battlefield and agree terrain definitions.
  4. ④ Determine starting crews and reinforcements.
  5. ⑤ Apply battlefield effects.
  6. ⑥ Take one base tactic; the lower-Rating gang gains one per 200-credit difference. Each tactic is once per battle.
  7. ⑦ Deploy starting with the defender.
N26 · Battle

Battle round and End phase

  1. Priority: Ready all models and roll off with D6. Reroll first-round ties; later ties favour the previous non-priority player.
  2. Action: starting with priority, alternate activating one Ready model.
  3. End: bottle checks → victory/objectives → reinforcements.
  4. Make a bottle check using the highest eligible Ld only if the gang suffered OOA this round.
  5. Withdraw one on failure, two on natural 12. Do not choose an engaged model first while an unengaged friendly remains.
N26 · Battle

Action allowance and repetition

  1. A normal activation grants two actions; Suppressed normally grants one.
  2. Single costs 1 / Double 2 / Free 0.
  3. Finish one action before declaring the next.
  4. Without an explicit exception, use the same named action only once per activation, even if its type changes.
The precise timing for removing the Suppressed marker remains for review.
N26 · Battle

Active model actions

  1. Move: Single, M inches. Run: Double, M+I inches.
  2. Shoot: Single, non-Heavy. Aimed Shoot: Double, non-Heavy, +1 to hit.
  3. Braced Shoot: Double, Heavy weapon.
  4. Charge: Double, M+D6 inches. Engage: Single, D6 inches. On success, Free Fight or Last Blow.
  5. Group Activation, Interact, Last Blow, Reload, Treat Ally, Repair and Sabotage: each Single.
  6. Vehicle All Guns Blazing: Double, all ranged weapons; declare every target before rolling.

Core action reference

ActionAction typeDistance / modifier
ShootSingle—
Aimed ShootDouble+1
Braced ShootDouble—
MoveSingleM
RunDoubleM+I
ChargeDoubleM+D6
EngageSingleD6
All Guns BlazingDouble—
N26 · Battle

Engaged and seriously injured/damaged actions

  1. Engaged: Fight Double or Retreat Double, I inches.
  2. Seriously Injured Fighter: Crawl Double, S inches / action for +1 recovery die / Desperate Escape.
  3. Seriously Damaged Vehicle: +1 recovery die / Desperate Escape / Freewheel Double, D6 inches.
  4. Desperate Escape: OOA, rolling lasting injury/damage on D6 1–2.
N26 · Battle

Movement and terrain costs

  1. Normally do not enter within 1 inch of an enemy. Check exceptions for Charge, Engage, Retreat, Crawl and seriously injured enemies.
  2. Difficult terrain: spend 2 inches per inch. Dangerous terrain: same cost plus a dangerous hit on D6 1 after crossing.
  3. Dangerous hit: automatic wound, no save, L1.
  4. Climbing: 2 inches per vertical inch. Ladders/stairs avoid doubled cost. Steps up to 0.5 inches are free.
  5. Add obstacle height and do not finish on it. Gaps up to 2 inches are automatic; wider gaps require Dexterity.
  6. During movement, open or close a door within 1 inch for 2 inches of movement each.
Needs review: the movement entry records 1-inch reach and 2-inch movement cost, but the basic door entry still marks operation range/cost unresolved. Agree the application with the Arbitrator.
N26 · Battle

Dexterity and falling

  1. Dexterity: D6 4+, Escher +1. Natural 1 fails and 6 succeeds.
  2. Railings give Fighters +1 Dexterity for fall risk. Successful voluntary descent reduces the effect one band.
  3. Under 3 inches: Suppressed.
  4. 3–6 inches: Suppressed plus an automatic wound, no save, L1 hit.
  5. Over 6 inches: OOA. A fall during the model’s activation ends it.
  6. Flying ignores fall damage and fall Suppression.
N26 · Battle

Shooting sequence

  1. ① Declare the weapon profile and enemy in line of sight.
  2. ② Measure range including height. Out of range fails.
  3. ③ Test BS to hit. Natural 1 fails and 6 succeeds; seriously injured target −1.
  4. ④ Against an engaged target, randomly allocate hits among that engagement’s participants.
  5. ⑤ Check Firepower, ammunition and traits, then resolve each hit’s wound, save and effects.
  6. ⑥ Hit models are normally Suppressed; check fall risk near edges.

N26 · Battle

Rapid Fire, ammo and Reload

  1. Rapid Fire (X): choose up to X Firepower dice; bullets determine hits.
  2. At least one ammo symbol: that profile is Out of Ammo. Two or more: unusable for the battle.
  3. A failed Ammo test adds one ammo symbol, not another Firepower die.
  4. Before wound rolls, allocate extra hits to eligible enemies within 3 inches of the original target and within range and sight.
  5. Reload Single restores one profile. Check Scarce, Limited, Single Shot and other exceptions.
  6. Melee attacks with a Light weapon do not use these Rapid Fire dice.
Needs review: extra rolls and Reload interactions involving Ammo(X+) and Out of Ammo remain unresolved. Do not infer extra dice or automatic restoration beyond the verified ammo-symbol rule.
N26 · Battle

Blast, template and optional shooting rules

  1. Blast affects the same level and retains its height after scattering.
  2. Check friendly and enemy engagement participants hit by a blast or template.
  3. A Template automatically hits touched models without a hit roll.
  4. Optional Target Priority: the closest enemy within 12 inches and sight; a successful Cool check can bypass it.
  5. Agree the unresolved scope before using optional Stray Shots.
The reference point for the 1-inch Stray Shots distance remains for review.
N26 · Battle

Close combat sequence

  1. ① Identify the active model and engaged enemy participants.
  2. ② Active model: one primary plus one allowed secondary. Inactive participant: one primary.
  3. ③ Active primary uses A attacks, +1 if charged this activation; secondary 1; inactive model 1. Light maximum 1.
  4. ④ Highest modified I first. Charge gives I+2; Unwieldy sets I1 before other modifiers. Ties are simultaneous.
  5. ⑤ Assistance +1, interference −1, unseen at declaration −1; check each condition.
  6. ⑥ Roll WS by weapon and target, then resolve wound, save and injury.
  7. ⑦ If all engaged enemies are OOA or seriously injured/damaged, consolidate I inches, ending at least 1 inch from every enemy.
The WS/BS exception for Light ranged weapons in melee remains for review.
N26 · Reference

Wound target table

  1. S ≥ 2×T → 2+. Example: S6 versus T3.
  2. T < S < 2×T → 3+. Example: S4 versus T3.
  3. S = T → 4+. Example: S3 versus T3.
  4. T/2 < S < T → 5+. Example: S3 versus T4.
  5. S ≤ T/2 → 6+. Example: S3 versus T6.
  6. Check traits such as Gas, Toxin and Shock for changes to this procedure.

N26 · Reference

Saves, cover and AP

  1. Choose at most one saving throw per successful wound.
  2. Normal save: D6 + AP + permitted modifiers ≥ Sv. Read AP “–” as 0.
  3. Ranged cover: +1 save at short range, +2 at long range.
  4. Invulnerable ignores AP, cover and all modifiers. Natural 1 and 2 fail all saves.
  5. Example: Sv 5+, AP−1 and short-range cover +1 requires a D6 of 5+.
  6. Do not bypass a no-save effect through another save or modifier.
N26 · Battle

W and Lethality L

  1. Normally lose 1 W per unsaved wound, to a minimum of 0. Check exceptions such as Damage (X).
  2. Roll L injury dice when W reaches or is already at 0.
  3. Choose one injury-die result and discard the others.
  4. Apply Injured/Damaged, Seriously Injured/Damaged or OOA. Repeated serious injury adds no extra effect.
  5. OOA removes the model from the battlefield; check lasting injury/damage.
  6. Do not substitute N26 L for N23 Damage.
Needs review: the relationship between W lost, L and injury dice for Damage(X) needs separate verification. Do not infer the exception from the basic L procedure.
N26 · Battle

Recovery, treatment and Last Blow

  1. If the activation began Seriously Injured/Damaged, make a recovery test at its end.
  2. An enemy within 1 inch that is not seriously injured/damaged causes OOA without the roll.
  3. One unengaged, not seriously injured friendly Fighter within 1 inch can assist for +1 die. Beasts/Vehicles cannot assist; Vehicles cannot receive it.
  4. The controller chooses one result from multiple recovery dice.
  5. Treat Ally/Repair Single: give a target within 1 inch an immediate recovery test.
  6. Last Blow Single: against a seriously injured enemy within 1 inch, win or tie D6+S to cause OOA.
N26 · Battle

Nerve, objectives and voluntary fleeing

  1. Friendly OOA within 3 inches → Cool check; failure Suppresses. Check Leader LOS12-inch or Champion LOS6-inch Cool support.
  2. Within 3 inches of objective centre: at least one non-Pet friendly Fighter and no enemy models; ignore serious injury/damage.
  3. Vehicles/Pets cannot control but can contest.
  4. Objective XP goes to one chosen controller, with at most one objective XP per Fighter per battle.
  5. Once ceil(1/3) of starting crew is OOA/withdrawn, voluntary fleeing is available at victory check start, causing automatic defeat.
N26 · Reference

States versus conditions

  1. Exclusive state priority: seriously injured/damaged → engaged → Suppressed → Active.
  2. Multiple conditions can coexist. Out of Ammo belongs to the affected profile.
  3. Injured/Damaged at W0 prevents skill use; remove when W recovers to at least 1.
  4. Webbed: cannot move, −1 to hit; remove on a successful Strength check at activation end.
  5. Intoxicated: WS/BS worsen by 1 (worst 6+), Cool +1 (maximum 10).
N26 · Battle

Wyrd manifestation, disruption and control

  1. Pay the power’s action cost and check Willpower. Concentrate Single gives +1 manifestation Wil this activation.
  2. Maintain Control Single: Wil+3, lasting until next activation end on success; ends immediately on failure.
  3. Free control at activation start: unmodified check; no other manifestation that activation regardless of success.
  4. One disruptor: enemy Wyrd within 18 inches and sight, Active/Suppressed and not Injured. Success gives manifesting Wil−2.
  5. Manifestation natural 2: automatic power then Perils. Natural 12: automatic failure then Perils. Disruption natural 2/12 also causes Perils.
  6. Weapons created by Wyrd powers ignore ammo symbols.
N26 · Post-battle

Post-battle checklist

  1. ① Models ending/withdrawing seriously injured/damaged: D6 3+ survive; 1–2 OOA and a lasting result.
  2. ② Award staked territory to the winner; on a draw retain previous ownership/unoccupied state.
  3. ③ Collect campaign rewards. Equipment goes to stash; apply Reputation gains before losses, minimum 1.
  4. ④ Record equipment recovery eligibility and XP.
  5. ⑤ Report gangs, outcome, territories and each gang’s inflicted enemy OOA.
N26 · Post-battle

Battle XP awards

  1. Participation +1 XP.
  2. Direct serious injury from own action +1 or direct OOA +2. Do not stack for the same enemy in one activation.
  3. Add +1 for a Leader, Champion, Brute or Vehicle target.
  4. Successful assistance to another Fighter’s recovery +1; Vehicles cannot assist or receive assistance.
  5. End-phase objective control +1, once per Fighter per battle; excludes Vehicles/Pets.
  6. Record cumulative XP; N26 advancements do not spend it.
N26 · Campaign

Post-cycle order

  1. ① One action per model that is neither Recovery nor Critical.
  2. ② Income and boons from controlled territories + Reputation×10 credits.
  3. ③ Roster update: advancements/promotions → trading post → equipment redistribution → cleanup.
  4. Work Territory: up to five Leaders/Champions/Gangers/Prospects, 15 credits each.
  5. Train: eligible model gains 2 XP. Develop Tactics: Leader/Champion creates one tactic.
  6. Finally clear all Recovery and remove dead, destroyed and retired models.
N26 · Campaign

Medical, bionic and repair costs

  1. Medical Escort: Leader/Champion escorts one Critical Fighter; pay 30 credits at roster update start or the target dies.
  2. Medical D6: 1 dies /2–3 lasting injury with tens die 5 /4–6 Recovery. Buy +1 per 50 credits before rolling.
  3. Bionics: Leader/Champion, 50 credits per lasting injury, including each duplicate; cannot remove Critical.
  4. A bionics target cannot take another post-cycle action or also receive Medical Escort that sequence.
  5. Chop Shop: 50 credits per Vehicle lasting damage instance, including duplicates.
N26 · Campaign

Advancement, promotion and caps

  1. Advance at post-cycle when cumulative XP enters a new band. Starting XP does not generate advancements.
  2. Thresholds: 4, 7, 10, 13, 19, 25, 31, 37, 49, 61, 73, 85, 97, 109, 121, 133, 157, 181, 205, 229.
  3. Prospect XP13+: replace the advancement roll with Ganger/Specialist, a specialisation/free skill and value+15.
  4. Ganger XP37+: after rolling advancement, replace Ganger with Champion; retain other subtypes/named type.
  5. Caps: M12 inches, WS/BS2+, S/T/W/I/A and mental stats 10, Sv 3+. Explicit exceptions override.
The first advancement from XP0 and cross-row advancement choice direction remain for review.

N26 · Campaign

Trade, weapon slots and equipment sets

  1. The gang equipment list is always accessible. External trading needs at least one Visit Trading Post action.
  2. Spend both credits and TP per transaction. Unused TP expires at the end of trading.
  3. Buy or transfer exclusive E only if on that model’s list.
  4. Fighters: 3 weapon slots, starred weapons 2, grenades excluded, one accessory per weapon. Vehicles use individual limits.
  5. Additional sets cost 0. Shared items count once for purchase/Rating; all cards share XP/injuries; one set per battle.
  6. Sell stash items for half their value, minimum 5 credits.
TP generation, odd-price sale rounding and random card-pool construction remain for review.
N26 · Setup

Gang creation, composition and finance

  1. Default budget 1000 credits, adjustable by the Arbitrator. Retain campaign leftovers; lose skirmish leftovers.
  2. Exactly one Leader. Champions+Brutes+Hangers-on ≤ other model count, excluding Pets. Check gang exceptions.
  3. Rating=sum of model values. Wealth=Rating+unused credits+stash equipment values.
  4. Reputation starts at 1, minimum 1, separate from Rating.
Rating exceptions for Captured or inactive models remain for review.
N26 · Campaign

Lasting injury, Recovery and capture

  1. For each campaign OOA event, the opponent rolls D66 lasting injury/Vehicle damage. Multiple simultaneous causes still mean one roll.
  2. Recovery prevents remaining battles that cycle and post-cycle actions; clear it at roster update.
  3. Captured escape D6: 1 dead/destroyed and removed.
  4. 2–4: pay D6×10 ransom at roster update for Recovery; otherwise remove and transfer equipment to captor’s stash.
  5. 5–6: escape and enter Recovery.
N26 · Setup

Mounted, Vehicle and Transport limits

  1. Choose Mounted use before crew selection; no dismounting in battle, wall/ladder climbing or melee secondary weapon.
  2. Default Mounted charges/runs move forwards with one 90-degree turn. Check explicit movement-subtype exceptions.
  3. Transport(X): capacityX, at least one entry; Brutes/Mounted cannot embark.
  4. Embark/disembark by Interact within 1 inch of entry, exiting at least 1 inch from enemies. No additional embark/disembark Interact that activation.
  5. Reinforcement Vehicles cannot begin with passengers. Embarked models receive Ready markers but may only Interact.
N26 · Campaign

Core Campaign overview

  1. Seven cycles: Occupation 3→Downtime 1→Takeover 3. Start with one Settlement plus one random territory.
  2. Occupation victory: 2D3×10 credits and Reputation+1. Defeat/draw/Side Job: D3×10.
  3. Takeover victory: 2D6×10 credits and Reputation+2. Defeat/draw/Side Job: D6×10. Losing territory costs 1 Reputation.
  4. Downtime 250 credits are only for new recruits/gang equipment; unused credits are lost.
  5. For Triumphs use each criterion, then Wealth to break ties, then shared awards. An enduring gang uses one boon for the next campaign only.
Needs review: the relationship between player count, total territory count and a separate 2D6 notation is unresolved. Distinguish D66 territory types from the number in the territory pool and agree with the Arbitrator.

N26 · Reference

D6 Perils of the Warp results

  1. 1: attempt a Free manifestation, with possible further Perils. Afterwards end activation, Suppress and suffer S4/AP−4/L1 hit.
  2. 2: move D6 inches in the scatter direction; falling is possible.
  3. 3: Ammo(X+)/Rapid Fire(X) weapons on all models within 3 inches become Out of Ammo.
  4. 4: gain Insane.
  5. 5: centred 5-inch blast; hit models suffer S5/AP−2/L1 and Suppression. The Wyrd is OOA.
  6. 6: M/S/T/A each+3, WS2+. OOA at next round’s End phase start or when this result recurs.
N26 · Reference

Complete D66 lasting injury table

  1. 11: Lesson Learnt — Gain D3 XP.
  2. 12: Eternal Enmity — Gain Hatred against the gang type responsible.
  3. 13: Bitter Enmity — Gain Hatred against the gang responsible.
  4. 14: Personal Enmity — Gain Hatred against the enemy model responsible. If no enemy model’s action caused the injury, gain Hatred against the gang instead.
  5. 15: Horrid Scars — Gain the Fearsome condition.
  6. 16: Impressive Scars — Improve Leadership by 1.
  7. 21-26: Out Cold — Remove from this battle with no lasting effects.
  8. 31-46: Grievous Wound — Go Into Recovery.
  9. 51: Eye Injury — Go Into Recovery and worsen Ballistic Skill by one step.
  10. 52: Hand Injury — Go Into Recovery and worsen Weapon Skill by one step.
  11. 53: Hobbled — Go Into Recovery and reduce Movement by 1.
  12. 54: Spinal Injury — Go Into Recovery and reduce Strength by 1.
  13. 55: Enfeebled — Go Into Recovery and reduce Toughness by 1.
  14. 56: Head Injury — Go Into Recovery and reduce Leadership by 1.
  15. 61-62: Captured — Become Captured and resolve the post-battle escape and ransom procedures.
  16. 63-65: Critical Injury — Become critically injured. Unless successfully treated during the post-cycle sequence, this fighter dies.
  17. 66: Memorable Death — Die immediately. If an enemy model caused the death, that model gains one additional XP.
This is the Fighter table; do not use it for Vehicle lasting damage. D3 conversion remains for review.

Glossary

Model
An umbrella term for Fighters and Vehicles. Mounted individuals are Fighters, not Vehicles.
Fighter
A model category distinct from Vehicles. A rule naming Fighters does not automatically apply to Vehicles.
Subtype
A model may have multiple classifications for roles, movement and other rules, separate from its display name.
Test
A roll that succeeds by reaching or exceeding the target.
Check
A roll that succeeds by being at or below the target.
Line of sight
An unobstructed line between model bodies, excluding decoration, barrels and bases.
Cover
Partial obstruction of the target body from the shooter, giving ranged saving throw modifiers.
Ready
The marker received in Priority that identifies models available for alternating activation.
Activation
A model’s turn to resolve actions in order, normally with two actions.
Single
An action type costing one action.
Double
An action type costing two actions.
Free
An action type costing no actions. The same-name restriction still needs checking.
Engaged
A close-contact state; Vehicles have a separate engagement choice within 1 inch.
Suppressed
A battle state normally limiting the next activation to one action.
Seriously Injured
A Fighter battle state distinct from Injured and campaign Recovery.
Out of Action
A result removing the model from battle; campaigns require checking lasting injury/damage.
Lethality L
In N26, the number of injury dice rolled when W reaches or is already 0.
AP
A weapon modifier applied to a normal save D6; ignored by Invulnerable saves.
Recovery
A campaign condition blocking later battles that cycle and post-cycle actions until roster updating.
Rating
The total credit value of gang models.
Wealth
Model values plus unused credits and stash equipment values.
Reputation
A gang value separate from Rating, starting/minimum 1 and used for income.
XP
Cumulative experience in N26, not spent; entering a new band triggers advancement procedures.
Advancement
Characteristic/skill and value changes gained in post-cycle for newly entered XP bands.
Promotion
The procedure for changing Prospect/Ganger subtypes at the required XP and timing.
Stash
The gang record for unused credits and equipment, used for rewards, sales and redistribution.
Trade Points TP
An N26 trading resource spent with credits; unused points expire at trading’s end.
Post-battle
The shared post-game sequence for territory, rewards, cleanup and reporting.
Post-cycle
The campaign sequence for model actions, income and roster updating.
